carmen: quick heads-up from an onboarding smoke for axon-embed-1280 (1.28k dim) against the anchor-holdout. ran 4-fold stratified eval comparing float32 / per-channel int8 / custom int6. seeing an odd failure mode isolated to the int6 path on the anchor cohort (high-precision anchors). posting notes + numbers.

mitesh: numbers plz

carmen: recall table (R@1, R@5, R@10) for overall vs anchor cohort (anchor = high-quality curated pairs):
```
overall (float / int8 / int6): 0.62 / 0.60 / 0.41
anchor  (float / int8 / int6): 0.86 / 0.84 / 0.22  <-- big drop
non-anchor: 0.58 / 0.57 / 0.52
```

signe: yikes. int6 only failing on anchor implies quant error that disproportionately affects high-similarity vectors. did you check L2 norm distributions?

carmen: yes. L2 norms (anchor queries): float mean=1.03 std=0.07, int8 mean=1.00 std=0.08, int6 mean=0.09 std=0.05. looks like near-zero collapse in int6 for anchor queries.

harper: that's symptomatic of double-scaling or a mistaken symmetric/asymmetric mapping in the custom int6 packer. which export path did you use?

carmen: flow: PyTorch -> scripted -> ONNX (opset 14) -> custom int6 converter (our internal quant lib) that packs 6-bit into bytes for runtime. for int8 we use ONNX quantize_static with per-channel weight quant + activation calib. int6 path uses a post-ONNX transform that rewrites some `Gemm` nodes and injects scale factors.

mitesh: did you run the int6 builder with a calibration set?

carmen: yes, used 4k calibration examples. but digging into per-op scales I found that certain linear layers have their scale applied twice during the rewriter pass for nodes fused by ONNX export. that double-application causes small outputs and eventual embedding collapse for inputs with narrow activation range (which anchors tend to have because they are semantically tight).

signe: can you paste a small diagnostic snippet for a failing anchor pair (float_cos vs int6_cos)?

carmen: sample:
```
anchor_q1: float_cos(p1)=0.92  int8_cos=0.89  int6_cos=0.08
anchor_q2: float_cos(p1)=0.88  int8_cos=0.86  int6_cos=0.11
anchor_q3: float_cos(p1)=0.90  int8_cos=0.87  int6_cos=0.07
```

harper: confirmed. please add a quick norm histogram and per-op scale dump to the eval artifacts. that'll make it easy to see which nodes had scale duplication.

embed-bot: auto-repro job started (job id eb-4410003210-01). ran per-channel int6 with patched rewriter (removed duplicate scale application) and static calibration. quick results: patched int6 anchor R@10=0.80, overall int6=0.79. artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/eb-4410003210/patch-run-01.zip

mitesh: great find. so root cause: rewriter bug not quant math per se. good that per-channel + static + rewriter fix recovers. what's the proposed onboarding change?

signe: propose three immediate changes: 1) block custom low-bit paths from auto-promotion unless they pass an "anchor parity" check (anchor R@10 within 0.95 of float), 2) require per-op scale-dump artifact in quant pipeline for all non-standard quantizers, 3) add an "anchor-set" regression test to kfold harness (flag: --anchor-set s3://...) that runs before any canary.

carmen: i'll open a PR to add the anchor-set flag + norm/scale dump and attach the failing-op list to artifacts. also will include an optional `--reject-if-anchor-drop>0.05` threshold.

harper: canary-bot: pausing scheduled canary rollout of axon-embed-1280-int6 across dedicated pools until post-quant parity gates pass. ticket AX-5012. @carmen pls mark when gates clear. :lock: 

embed-bot: summary numbers (float / patched-int6 / int8): overall 0.62 / 0.79 / 0.60, anchor 0.86 / 0.80 / 0.84. note: patched-int6 slightly overshoots float on some anchor microclusters; investigating tiny calibration bias. full artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/eb-4410003210/summary.csv

mitesh: followups: 1) add a CI gate that fails if mean_intX_norm < 0.6 * mean_float_norm per cohort (anchor + short + longtail), 2) retrain PQ/IVF on dequantized quant outputs when promoting low-bit builds, 3) run a small A/B offline user-quality check on a held-out anchor set before traffic split.

signe: agree. I'll own PQ retrain automation. carmen pls ping when the PR for the harness lands.

carmen: will do. thanks all for the quick turnaround. closing thread once PR merged + canary unpaused. :coffee:
